newsitem.title: USA: Chicago-area school adopts racially charged name.
newsitem.headline: Chicago-area school adopts racially charged name.

text.p: A Chicago area school has decided to adopt the name "Redskins," a name American Indians consider derogatory, officials said Thursday.

McHenry County District 158 school board last week approved changing Huntley Middle School's team name to Redskins from Royals, principal Terry Awrey said. There are no known American Indian students at Huntley Middle School, where students voted by a comfortable margin to adopt the new name.
"It has not become an issue here in Huntley," Awrey said.

But Candice Esquivel, an Ojibway Indian and executive director of the American Indian Centre in Chicago, objected to the name, saying, "Redskin where I come from is a derogatory term ... We just find it demeaning."
American Indians have made many protests at sporting events such as the World Series and the Super Bowl, complaining about nicknames such as "Indians" and "Redskins."

Awrey said the change was prompted by a planned relocation of the school this summer to shared quarters with Huntley High School, whose team name was already the Redskins. "Everything we're doing will be positive and show respect and honour for Native Americans," he said.

Two other schools in the Chicago area have dropped the name Redskins because it was viewed as a racial slur. Naperville Central High School changed its team name to Redhawks from Redskins and Marist High School on the city's South Side is dropping Redskins and looking for a new name.
In Oxford, Ohio, Miami University will adopt the name Redhawks on July 1, ending its use of the Redskins moniker.
